tasks.reason: The retrieval extractor in src/catalog/nvidia-nim.ts recognized only one hard-coded route shape, so two classes of reviewed first-party documents were dropped even though each document's request schema independently names the model. exactRoutes compared per-model rerank routes with a literal path === `/retrieval/${id}/reranking`, but NVIDIA's registry uses page slugs that spell the model ID's dots as underscores (page `nvidia-llama-3_2-nv-rerankqa-1b-v2` for model `nvidia/llama-3.2-nv-rerankqa-1b-v2`), so three rerankers were rejected. It also treated every retrieval-host route as reranking, so the retrieval-host embeddings route (`/retrieval/snowflake/arctic-embed-l/embeddings`) was rejected even though parseNvidiaNimRetrieval already handles embeddings-only fields. Repair: a new retrievalTask(path, id) helper matches `^/retrieval/PUBLISHER[/SLUG]/TASK$` for tasks reranking|embeddings, keeps the generic `/retrieval/nvidia/reranking` form reranking-only, and for per-model routes requires the underscore-normalized publisher/slug to equal the underscore-normalized model ID; the request schema's model default/example/enum must still independently name id, so no endpoint, modality or price is inferred. exactRoutes now maps that task to Rerank or Embeddings and uses the retrieval host for those routes. Replaying the identical saved bundle moves parsed models from 14 to 18, adding exactly nvidia/llama-3.2-nv-rerankqa-1b-v1, nvidia/llama-3.2-nv-rerankqa-1b-v2, nvidia/llama-3.2-nemoretriever-500m-rerank-v2 and nvidia/snowflake/arctic-embed-l, which were previously absent from data/catalog.json. Deliberate rejections are preserved: nvidia-nemotron-3_5-parse-infer (localhost server, non-embedding path) and nvidia-nv-rerankqa-mistral-4b-v3-infer (generic route whose example names nvidia/rerank-qa-mistral-4b, a different model) still yield no claim. Residual omission: the admitted HTTP 404 for the linked document nvidia-nim-retrieval/nvidia-embedding-2b-infer is a source gap, not a parser defect; nvidia/embed-qa-4 keeps its other documented claim (the Build endpoint supplement) and no endpoint, modality or price is invented for the removed document. This repair does not restore that document and does not establish the completeness of NVIDIA's published inventory beyond the documents the reviewed index links.

The manifest path regex, allowedHosts and suffix therefore still match the index; only the document target is gone, so nvidia-nim-retrieval/nvidia-embedding-2b-infer records fetch_failed/HTTP 404 with impact claim. The parser's documented behavior for a removed linked document is to make no claim, which this run keeps: inventing the missing endpoint, modality or price would fabricate evidence.
